founded.text: On Christmas Day 1886 Matt Hammond hauled a wagon of lumber onto the old cattle roundup ground to put up the town's first buildings.

timeline.text: By spring, hundreds of men were at work on the irrigation system meant to bring water to the valley.
The stone block at the corner of Main and Market was completed.
The Rio Grande Southern reached Dolores; the spur to Cortez was never completed.
The Mesa Verde area was designated a national park.
Storms on July 10 washed out the flumes and much of the irrigation system.
